title: Solar Constant to Ground: Where the Energy Goes
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Follow 1361 W/m2 down through the atmosphere, losing a named and quantified amount at every stage, until you arrive at whatever your station actually reads.

educational.topic: Solar Constant to Ground: Where the Energy Goes
learningObjectives: Attribute the difference between the solar constant and ground irradiance to specific causes.
Quantify the contribution of zenith angle, absorption, scattering, cloud and albedo.
prerequisites: Chapter 9 sections on the solar constant

keyQuestions: Your station reads 700 W/m2 at noon. Is something wrong?
Why is the loss to the angle bigger in December than in June?
What does air mass 2 mean physically?
commonMisconceptions: Believing seasons are caused by distance from the Sun.
Expecting a ground sensor to read anywhere near 1361 W/m2.
Treating cloud as the only reason irradiance is low.
assessmentOpportunities: Attributes a measured irradiance to named causes with numbers attached.
Explains why air mass matters and why it grows non-linearly.
States that a low reading is usually geometry and weather rather than a fault.
